provenance.prompt:
Create a crisp pixel-art atlas on a fully transparent background, exactly SIX COLUMNS by SIX ROWS, no text or borders. Columns in exact order FRONT, TOP, RIGHT, LEFT, BOTTOM, REAR. Rows in exact order faction-larracos-larracos-college-of-magic-entrance; iron-tracks-tunnel-stone-open-doorway; hunting-jungle-vine-covered-ruin-stone-open-doorway; industry-menagerie-soot-stained-brick-open-doorway; faction-battlefield-fortified-camp-gate; early-arenas-gated-stone-bridge. The attached contact sheet has a canonical SOURCE followed by current views in each row; the SOURCE is the authority for that row’s material, ornament, count, and open/closed state. Preserve source identity exactly; never borrow another row’s motifs. True orthographic axis-aligned views only, no isometric or perspective. FRONT/REAR are straight elevations with no visible top; TOP looks straight down and BOTTOM straight up; RIGHT/LEFT are edge-on side elevations. Keep consistent physical proportions across directions. Each cell contains one object, centered, separated with transparent margin; no detached specks or neighboring-cell overlap.

ROW 1 faction-larracos-larracos-college-of-magic-entrance: pale carved stone arch with blue magical inset and paired small statues. TOP must be the full shallow arch, pillar, statue-base footprint seen from directly above, with no frontal arch face; BOTTOM is the matching pale-stone foundation underside, same complete footprint, no generic square panel. Preserve paired statues; do not invent posts or extra objects.

ROW 2 iron-tracks-tunnel-stone-open-doorway: open stone tunnel portal with moss and dark passage. TOP is only the shallow lintel and post-cap surfaces in plan, with dark opening empty; BOTTOM is the matching threshold/foot underside, not a frontal wall with stacked masonry courses. Preserve visible opening and source moss/stone.

ROW 3 hunting-jungle-vine-covered-ruin-stone-open-doorway: open overgrown stone doorway with vines. TOP is a compact orthographic arch/frame footprint with thin vine and stone edge details, not a floor tile; BOTTOM is the matching stone foundation underside. REAR shows the reverse side of the same open through-passage: paired jambs and arch, empty opening, not a sealed masonry wall.

ROW 4 industry-menagerie-soot-stained-brick-open-doorway: open soot-dark brick and stone arch with steel corner braces. TOP is a shallow arch-lintel plan with cap stones above the passage, not an upright frontal arch; BOTTOM is a matching narrow foundation/threshold underside, not the front door face. REAR is the reverse elevation with the same open passage, no brick wall closing it. Keep the source dark red brick and gray stone.

ROW 5 faction-battlefield-fortified-camp-gate: rough timber gate with two posts, beam, hanging green cloth banners and rocks. TOP has the gate beam and two post caps/rocks as an overhead footprint; hanging cloth presents as thin hems, not broad flag faces. BOTTOM has timber post-foot undersides and ground-anchored structure at the same footprint, not a generic full square ground patch. Preserve the source two-post count and green cloth.

ROW 6 early-arenas-gated-stone-bridge: dark timber bridge deck between pale stone posts and railings. FRONT/REAR are bridge-end elevations with the deck edge and paired stone posts, not the overhead walkway tilted upright. RIGHT/LEFT are long low side elevations with horizontal bridge deck and railing spans along X, coherent with the source plan. Keep the same count of stone posts, no additional gates or panels.
